subject.title: security: deny-all top-level token permissions on release workflows; maintainer-skill temp-file hygiene

question: Should release owners accept this PR's six workflow-level `permissions: {}` additions despite the related closed decision that the same six workflows already have explicit job permissions and no effective current restriction is added?
rationale: The source audit is strong, but ordinary PR CI does not exercise maintainer release dispatches, and a related maintainer decision already questioned this exact hardening unit.

options.title: Split workflow defaults out
options.body: Land or continue reviewing the maintainer-skill hygiene while removing the six workflow-level defaults unless a release owner sponsors them separately.

options.title: Accept audited defaults
options.body: Merge the workflow defaults with explicit release-owner acceptance that all 40 jobs have job-level permissions and no live dispatch proof was run.

options.title: Run release preflight first
options.body: Have a release owner run a safe validation or preflight dispatch before merge to prove the new defaults against a real release workflow path.

recommendation.title: Split workflow defaults out
recommendation.body: Land or continue reviewing the maintainer-skill hygiene while removing the six workflow-level defaults unless a release owner sponsors them separately.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history across the touched release workflow family and release-control hardening commits.
